predecessor: REGISTRY-STRATEGY-DURABILITY-PREREQUISITE-001 (superseded; its command_contract.py/pg_store.py WIP added a second full-spec/revision authority and was never merged to dev, so it was not resumed unchanged)
scope_note: This delivery covers §3.1 (single durable write authority, fail-closed backend selection), §3.2 (frozen capability contract, the net-new update_metadata_cas capability with immutable-content protection, correct action-owner semantics for the BFF Strategy adapter, real checksum/version-lineage validation on StrategySpec registration), and §3.3 (CAS + atomic idempotent receipt scoped by tenant/actor/aggregate, auth enforcement across every Registry mutation route, verified-actor audit binding). A follow-up corrective pass (2026-09-06, responding to an independent Codex review of the prior generation) closed 7 must-fix findings: (1) auth was previously wired onto only the metadata route — every mutating route now calls _authenticate_registry_write and threads the verified actor into the write; (2) the metadata PATCH could silently overwrite an immutable strategy_spec/strategy_artifact/allocation_policy_artifact/source_seed_id payload — now rejected; (3) the StrategySpec registration facade accepted a mismatched checksum and an arbitrary out-of-sequence version with no parent linkage — both now rejected with real validation; (4) backend selection silently defaulted unset/empty REGISTRY_STORE_BACKEND to the in-memory store even in an enforced (staging/prod) persistence posture — now fails closed via services.foundation.persistence_posture, the same pattern every other owner service in this repo uses; (5) command-key replay returned the *current* entry state instead of the originally committed one, and the receipt key was not scoped by tenant/actor — both fixed, with a corrected assertion in test_registry_owner_transaction.py that previously asserted the wrong (stale) behavior; (6) the BFF StrategyCommandAdapter silently replaced the caller's CAS precondition with a fresh GET and manufactured its receipt from a second re-GET instead of the actual PATCH response — both fixed; (7) test_owner_durability.py's 'process restart' was an in-process singleton reset with a permissive stub token, not a real OS-process boundary with a strict JWT — a new module (test_owner_durability_real_process.py) adds a genuine subprocess/uvicorn-based two-process proof, gated the same way (TEST_DATABASE_URL) as the rest of this suite. Remaining, still-undelivered scope: real governance-review/promotion/runtime owner HTTP integration for submit_review/promote_paper/activate/pause/archive, and adversarial response-loss/outbox-crash-window injection (killing the server process mid-transaction) — both recorded honestly below, not claimed as done. architecture-resumption-sa-sd.md §4 explicitly permits Registry to merge before all consumers once its own required checks pass.

summary: PostgresRegistryStore (pg_store.py): durable RegistryEntry owner store using services/foundation/postgres_json_store.py's PostgresJsonOwnerStore. CAS-guarded update() binds the caller's base snapshot (not a fetch-immediately-before-write); commit_metadata_cas() reserves the (now tenant/actor/aggregate-scoped) command receipt *before* mutating the entry, using insert_if_absent's created/duplicate result to decide the control flow rather than assuming, and finalizes the receipt with the actual committed entry snapshot inside the same Postgres transaction — a same-key replay now returns that stored original snapshot, never a fresh read of whatever the row has become since under a later, unrelated command.

Fixed a latent concurrent-first-bootstrap race in postgres_json_store.ensure_postgres_schema/PostgresJsonOwnerStore.bootstrap (23505 unique-violation when two owner-store instances race their first CREATE SCHEMA/TABLE IF NOT EXISTS) — proven with a dedicated concurrency test against a real database, affects every consumer of this shared primitive.

storage.py: build_registry_store()/get_store() select memory (explicit test-only opt-in, documented in services/registry/conftest.py) vs postgres (REGISTRY_STORE_BACKEND=postgres). Backend selection now calls services.foundation.persistence_posture.require_persistence_posture (the same fail-closed pattern every other owner service in this repo already uses): an enforced (staging/prod) persistence posture with a non-postgres/unset backend raises RuntimeError before serving a request, instead of silently returning the in-memory store. Fixed a pre-existing aliasing bug: RegistryStore.get()/list_by_strategy() returned live references into the store's internal dict, so a caller mutating the returned object silently mutated durable state outside of update(); both now return copies, matching real backend semantics.

split_api.py: advance_artifact_state() and update_deployment_summary() now pass a base snapshot to store.update()/store.update_deployment_summary() and translate a stale-snapshot conflict into RegistryConflictError (HTTP 409) instead of an unconditional overwrite. Added update_metadata() — the 'allowed metadata update with CAS' capability required by architecture-resumption-sa-sd.md §3.2, including a command_key idempotent-replay path and a new immutable-content guard (_reject_immutable_metadata_mutation): once an entry's metadata carries a reserved key (strategy_spec/strategy_artifact/allocation_policy_artifact/source_seed_id), the generic metadata PATCH can no longer overwrite or remove it.

models.py: RegistryEntry gained last_actor (verified-caller audit binding: actor_id/roles/tenant/token_kind) so every mutation records who performed it, threaded through every store/service call site as an optional actor= parameter.

service.py: verified-caller auth (services/runtime_auth_inbound.validate_request_auth) is now called at the start of every mutating route — register_entry, register_strategy_spec, register_strategy_artifact, register_allocation_policy_artifact, every advance route, mutate_strategy_artifact_entry, and update_deployment_summary — not just the metadata PATCH route. A new _require_verified_identity check additionally rejects a signature-valid JWT that omits subject/tenant/role/expiry claims (structured legacy tokens used by this package's permissive-mode unit tests are exempt, since they carry no claims to omit). docker-compose.yml/docker-compose.control.yml already set PANTHEON_REGISTRY_AUTH_MODE=strict and REGISTRY_STORE_BACKEND=postgres for the registry service, so no compose changes were needed this pass. register_strategy_spec now also verifies a supplied checksum against the computed checksum of the supplied strategy_spec (rejecting a mismatch) and validates that a new version is either the first for its strategy_id, an idempotent replay of an existing version, a legitimate immediate-next semver bump, or declares parent_registry_ids linking it to an existing StrategySpec entry.

command_contract.py: canonical STRATEGY_ACTIONS matrix (unchanged this pass). update_params resolves to Registry's update_metadata_cas capability; submit_review/promote_paper/activate/pause/archive resolve to governance_review/promotion/runtime and carry no Registry capability, so a caller can no longer relabel one business action as another.

BFF strategy_adapter.py: _execute_update_params no longer overwrites the caller's expected_metadata CAS precondition with a freshly-fetched GET (that defeated CAS/lost-update protection) — the caller must supply expected_metadata and it passes through unchanged. The receipt is now built from the actual PATCH response (entry snapshot + X-Idempotent-Replay header) via the new http_request_json_with_headers helper, never from a second, independent GET; a PATCH response with no confirmable entry payload raises ActionUnavailableError(AMBIGUOUS_REGISTRY_RESPONSE) instead of manufacturing a false 'metadata_updated' success. submit_review/promote_paper/activate/pause/archive still raise ActionUnavailableError naming the exact non-Registry owner. RankingFormula/Ranking handling in the same file is untouched.

BFF base.py: added http_request_json_with_headers + header_value so a caller can inspect response headers (X-Idempotent-Replay) instead of only the parsed JSON body — needed for the strategy_adapter.py fix above. http_request_json's method dispatch fix (GET/POST/PATCH/DELETE sent as the requested verb, not silently coerced to POST) is unchanged from the prior generation.

No parallel full-spec/revision authority or duplicate route exists in the currently mounted app; the retirement inventory in first_release_contract.json documents this explicitly rather than claiming a retirement that was never needed.

New test_owner_durability_real_process.py: launches the mounted app via a real subprocess.Popen running uvicorn (not an in-process TestClient), authenticated with a strictly-signed HS256 JWT (issuer/audience/subject/tenant/role/expiry all present) through the real verifier. Proves (a) an entry registered by one OS process reads back correctly after that process is killed and a brand-new process is started against the same DSN/schema, and (b) two independent OS processes against the same Postgres backend show correct cross-process CAS rejection (409) and command-key replay (returns the originally committed value, not the row's current state). Gated on TEST_DATABASE_URL like every other Postgres-backed suite in this package; not executable in this sandbox (no live Postgres, and container/docker access to start one was not available in this session) — see not_covered_in_this_delivery.
